evidence.V1: Classic crown-over-pavilion gem outline reads at 64 px from front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view is a clear octagon; front outline symmetric, A15 X/Y error 0.0.
evidence.V2: Big crown/pavilion split and a medium girdle band plus 8 crown facets around a flat table, but no small-scale detail (no star/break facets, pavilion is one plain 8-sided cone), so all facets sit at about the same scale.
evidence.V3: Reads as a stylised gem with a chunky crown, but it is close to an octagonal frustum on a cone: the pavilion is a stiff primitive point and the crown-to-pavilion ratio has no exaggeration.
evidence.V4: Facet edges are crisp with no ~0.045 chamfer; only the thin girdle band softens the crown/pavilion break, so edges do not catch a highlight line the way the anchor's bevelled rim and star do.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (crown, pavilion, studio and flat) show clean planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray triangles; flipped_faces 0, cap_overlaps 0, self_intersections 0.
evidence.V6: A single hue in light/mid/dark values (table light, crown mid, pavilion near-black), and the crimson/royal colourways swap cleanly, so the palette is disciplined.
evidence.V7: 64 tris against a tiny-class target of 150 (ceiling 300).
evidence.V8: Uses the kit's one white material with vertex colours and a hue in 3 values, but has no kit-standard ~0.045 chamfers and is fully faceted rather than smooth with bevels: a minor mismatch.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box fidelity, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

top_fixes: Add a small ~0.045-stud chamfer to the girdle and to the table/crown edges so the facet breaks catch a light line and match the kit bevel standard
Add small-scale facets (star facets around the table, a split pavilion with break facets, or a culet tip) to give a third level of detail
Push the stylised proportion further, for example a wider, flatter table with a deeper and slightly tapered pavilion, so it reads less like a frustum on a cone
Lift the pavilion's darkest value slightly so the lower half does not drop to near-black under studio light
